newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids steady to up again on stable crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids steady to up again on stable crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to up slightly again Tuesday in sluggish trade, still supported by a stable-to-firm crude market despite forecasts for fairly mild East Coast weather this week.
"There's not a lot of load, but crude held up today and why should sellers discount just before the (summer cooling) season starts?" said one cash trader.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent inched up slightly to $15.50 a barrel, while June paper retreated slightly to the low-$16s after a sharp gain yesterday on the near-$1 gain in crude, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also gained slightly to $16.25, traders said.
New York high sulphurs again were unchanged on the day, with 2.2 percent still talked on either side of $14.50.

At the U.S. Gulf, three percent firmed 15 cents to $14.00-25 on reports a major sold late Monday 60,000 barrels of prompt 2.7 percent at $14.60 (FOB Miss. River). Traders said another prompt barge of 2.8 percent sold today at $14.50 (FOB Beaumont, Tx.).
USG one percent again held steady at $14.75.

New York city gate swing gas prices skidded about a dime Tuesday to the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or about $15.31 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, fell more than a nickel to $2.19/mmBtu, or $13.80 a barrel.
